src.label: Rosselkhoznadzor — instruction: how to bring a pet into Russia (in Russian)

head: Up to two dogs or cats need only an international veterinary passport, with rabies vaccination.
lines: Rosselkhoznadzor says up to two dogs or cats carried for personal use can enter the Eurasian Economic Union without its permit and without prior quarantine, provided they have an international veterinary passport that serves as the veterinary certificate.

The passport must show the vets' vaccination marks, a rabies vaccination for every carnivore, and a mark from your country's competent authority that a clinical exam took place within 14 days before departure. Vaccination is due at least 20 days before dispatch if none was given in the last 12 months.

A 3-year rabies vaccine is accepted if the vet confirms immunity is still valid, or a lab shows at least 0.5 IU/ml. Unvaccinated kittens and puppies under 3 months need veterinary certificate form 15. The same form 15 is needed if there is no passport or the pet travels without its owner.
